sentence: This project runs a reading and life science program in public libraries to help young children learn science and make healthy food choices.
This project uses a rat model of Alzheimer's disease to find the neural circuits behind lost motivation and to test whether function can be restored.
This project studies how the ubiquitin and autophagy pathways work in cells, using quantitative cell biological and proteomics approaches.
This project uses somatic mutations in diseased livers to find genetic pathways that may help liver health and to study how mutant clones expand.
This project studies whether mutations in inverted terminal repeat sequences of adeno-associated virus gene therapy vectors affect how stable and safe the therapeutic transgenes are.
This project studies how a protein that binds RNA links cell metabolism to RNA modifications that control gene expression in cancers such as acute leukemia.
This project studies how cancer, the immune response and scleroderma disease activity relate to each other in patients with scleroderma.
This project studies the role of cell surface proteins in how Candida auris causes disease and develops vaccine strategies.
This project studies how a protein that binds both RNA and DNA controls RNA editing and splicing of developmental genes as human cells change fate.
This project studies where pediatric radiation-induced gliomas come from, using patient-derived models to look at risk factors and treatment strategies.
This project identifies behaviors of concerned partners that relate to changes in a partner's drinking, then builds and tests a web-based intervention for them.
This project studies how voltage-gated sodium channels control renal vascular resistance and contribute to acute kidney injury in neonates.
This project studies neurons that carry corneal pain signals and how they change after corneal inflammation and nerve injury.
This project collects daily-life data from adults with obesity and pain to learn how stress leads to pain and obesity-maintaining behaviors.
This project builds chemical and imaging tools to link the genotype of single cells to organ-scale phenotype in the same tissue.
This project develops a way to deliver nanomedicines to the coronary microvasculature of human hearts during ex vivo normothermic perfusion, to treat ischemia-reperfusion injury.
This project studies how Clusterin helps the intestinal epithelium regrow after severe radiation injury in mouse and human intestinal organoids.
This project builds surface-based tools for fiber tracking to map the superficial white matter connectome from diffusion MRI brain images.
This project tests whether early changes in self-focused attention can predict which patients do not respond to cognitive behavioral therapy.
This project uses chemistry and mass spectrometry to make small molecules that help find and test molecular targets for drugs.
